topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: The circumferences of two circles are in the ratio $4:7$. The ratio of their radii is
answer: Correct option: C) $4:7$. $\frac{2\pi r_{1}}{2\pi r_{2}} = \frac{4}{7}$, so $r_{1}:r_{2} = 4:7$. ($16:49$ is the ratio of the areas.)

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: A semicircular protractor has diameter $d$. The area of its face is
answer: Correct option: B) $\frac{1}{8}\pi d^{2}$. Radius $= \frac{d}{2}$, so area $= \frac{1}{2}\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{\pi d^{2}}{8}$.

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: A semicircular flower bed has an area of $693\text{ m}^{2}$. The length of fencing needed to go all round its boundary is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: D) $108\text{ m}$. $\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{22}{7}r^{2} = 693$ gives $r^{2} = 441$, $r = 21\text{ m}$. Perimeter $= \pi r + 2r = 66 + 42 = 108\text{ m}$.

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: A circle and a semicircle have the same radius. The numerical value of the area of the circle equals the numerical value of the perimeter of the semicircle. Using $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, the diameter of the circle is
answer: Correct option: A) $\frac{36}{11}$ units. $\pi r^{2} = \pi r + 2r$ gives $r = 1 + \frac{2}{\pi} = 1 + \frac{7}{11} = \frac{18}{11}$, so diameter $= \frac{36}{11}$.

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: A wire of length $88\text{ cm}$ is first bent into a square and then rebent into a circle. The ratio of the area of the square to the area of the circle is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: C) $11:14$. Square: side $22\text{ cm}$, area $484\text{ cm}^{2}$. Circle: $2\pi r = 88$, $r = 14\text{ cm}$, area $616\text{ cm}^{2}$. $484:616 = 11:14$.

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text:
Assertion (A): A circular running track of circumference $132\text{ m}$ has a diameter of $21\text{ m}$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
Reason (R): The circumference of a circle of radius $r$ is $2\pi r$.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: D) A is false but R is true. $2\times\frac{22}{7}\times r = 132$ gives $r = 21\text{ m}$, so the diameter is $42\text{ m}$, not $21\text{ m}$. R is the correct formula.

topic: Circumference and area of a circle
text: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ so that all four vertices lie on the circle. The area of the square is
answer: Correct option: B) $72\text{ cm}^{2}$. The diagonal is a diameter, $12\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2}d^{2} = \frac{1}{2}\times 144 = 72\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The perimeter of a quadrant of a circle of radius $7\text{ cm}$ is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: C) $25\text{ cm}$. Arc $= \frac{1}{4}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 7 = 11\text{ cm}$. Perimeter $= 11 + 7 + 7 = 25\text{ cm}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A sector of a circle of radius $10\text{ cm}$ has area $25\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$. The central angle of the sector is
answer: Correct option: A) $90^\circ$. $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times\pi\times 100 = 25\pi$ gives $\theta = 90^\circ$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A sector of a circle with central angle $120^\circ$ has area $462\text{ cm}^{2}$. The radius of the circle is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: D) $21\text{ cm}$. $\frac{120}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}r^{2} = 462$ gives $r^{2} = 441$, $r = 21\text{ cm}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A circular pizza is cut through its centre into $10$ equal slices. The angle at the centre of each slice is
answer: Correct option: B) $36^\circ$. Each slice gets $\frac{360^\circ}{10} = 36^\circ$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$ is divided into $12$ equal sectors. The area of each sector is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: A) $115.5\text{ cm}^{2}$. Circle area $= \frac{22}{7}\times 441 = 1386\text{ cm}^{2}$; each sector $= \frac{1386}{12} = 115.5\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: In the figure, $O$ is the centre of a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$. The three shaded sectors have central angles $70^\circ$, $80^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. The total shaded area is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: C) $924\text{ cm}^{2}$. Total angle $= 240^\circ$. Area $= \frac{240}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 441 = \frac{2}{3}\times 1386 = 924\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The arc of a sector of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ is $33\text{ cm}$ long. The area of the sector is
answer: Correct option: D) $231\text{ cm}^{2}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2}lr = \frac{1}{2}\times 33\times 14 = 231\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The radius of a sector is made $3$ times and its central angle is made one-third. The area of the new sector is how many times the area of the original sector?
answer: Correct option: B) $3$. Area $\propto \theta r^{2}$: new area $= \frac{1}{3}\times 3^{2} = 3$ times the original.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The diagonals of a rhombus $ABCD$ intersect at $O$. With centre $O$ and radius $14\text{ cm}$, an arc is drawn from a point on $OA$ to a point on $OB$. The area of the sector so formed is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: C) $154\text{ cm}^{2}$. The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$. Area $= \frac{1}{4}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 196 = 154\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The perimeter of a sector of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ is $50\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the sector.
answer:
Perimeter $= 2r + l$, so $l = 50 - 28 = 22\text{ cm}$.
Area of sector $= \frac{1}{2}lr = \frac{1}{2}\times 22\times 14 = 154\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A flower bed in a park is in the shape of a sector of a circle of radius $10.5\text{ m}$ with central angle $120^\circ$. Find the length of the brick edging needed to go once around the whole bed. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Arc length $= \frac{120}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 10.5 = \frac{1}{3}\times 66 = 22\text{ m}$.
Edging $=$ arc $+ 2r = 22 + 21 = 43\text{ m}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The area of a sector of a circle is $231\text{ cm}^{2}$ and the length of its arc is $22\text{ cm}$. Find the radius of the circle and the angle of the sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Area $= \frac{1}{2}lr$: $231 = \frac{1}{2}\times 22\times r$, so $r = 21\text{ cm}$.
$l = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 2\pi r$: $22 = \frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 132$, so $\theta = 60^\circ$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: In a circle of radius $28\text{ cm}$, an arc subtends an angle of $45^\circ$ at the centre. Find the length of the arc and the area of the corresponding sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Arc length $= \frac{45}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 28 = \frac{1}{8}\times 176 = 22\text{ cm}$.
Area of sector $= \frac{45}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 28\times 28 = \frac{1}{8}\times 2464 = 308\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A chord of a circle of radius $28\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle at the centre. Find the areas of the minor sector and the major sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Area of circle $= \frac{22}{7}\times 28\times 28 = 2464\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Minor sector $= \frac{90}{360}\times 2464 = 616\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Major sector $= 2464 - 616 = 1848\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: A circular table top of diameter $70\text{ cm}$ is divided into $10$ equal sectors by lines through its centre. Find the area and the perimeter of one sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Radius $= 35\text{ cm}$; angle of each sector $= 36^\circ$.
Area $= \frac{1}{10}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 35\times 35 = \frac{3850}{10} = 385\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Arc $= \frac{1}{10}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 35 = 22\text{ cm}$, so perimeter $= 22 + 35 + 35 = 92\text{ cm}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: In the figure, $O$ is the centre of a circle of radius $7\text{ cm}$. The three shaded sectors have central angles $80^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. Find the total area of the shaded region. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Sum of the angles $= 80^\circ + 90^\circ + 100^\circ = 270^\circ$.
Shaded area $= \frac{270}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 7\times 7 = \frac{3}{4}\times 154 = 115.5\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Area and perimeter of a sector
text: The perimeter of a sector of a circle is $39\text{ cm}$ and its area is $77\text{ cm}^{2}$. The radius is a whole number of centimetres. Form a quadratic equation in the radius $r$ and solve it to find $r$. Hence find the length of the arc and the central angle of the sector. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Let the arc be $l$. Then $2r + l = 39$ and $\frac{1}{2}lr = 77$.
So $l = 39 - 2r$ and $r(39 - 2r) = 154$, giving $2r^{2} - 39r + 154 = 0$.
$r = \frac{39 \pm \sqrt{1521 - 1232}}{4} = \frac{39 \pm 17}{4}$, so $r = 14$ or $r = 5.5$.
The radius is a whole number, so $r = 14\text{ cm}$ and $l = 39 - 28 = 11\text{ cm}$.
$\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14 = 11$ gives $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 88 = 11$, so $\theta = 45^\circ$.

text: A circular window in a school hall has diameter $42\text{ cm}$. It is divided into $6$ equal sectors by $3$ steel strips along diameters, and a steel strip also runs along the whole circular rim. Two opposite sectors are fitted with coloured glass and the rest with clear glass, as shown in the figure. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

parts.label: (i)

parts.text: Find the total length of steel strip used.
parts.answer: Rim $= 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21 = 132\text{ cm}$; diameters $= 3\times 42 = 126\text{ cm}$. Total $= 258\text{ cm}$.

parts.answer: One sector $= \frac{60}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21\times 21 = \frac{1386}{6} = 231\text{ cm}^{2}$. Two sectors $= 2\times 231 = 462\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Arc length
text: An arc of length $11\text{ cm}$ lies on a circle of radius $21\text{ cm}$. The angle it subtends at the centre is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: A) $30^\circ$. $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21 = 11$ gives $\frac{\theta}{360^\circ}\times 132 = 11$, so $\theta = 30^\circ$.

topic: Arc length
text: A piece of wire $22\text{ cm}$ long is bent into an arc of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$. The angle subtended by the arc at the centre is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: D) $90^\circ$. Circumference $= 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14 = 88\text{ cm}$. $\theta = \frac{22}{88}\times 360^\circ = 90^\circ$.

topic: Arc length
text: An arc of a circle is $22\text{ cm}$ long and subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the centre. The radius of the circle is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: B) $21\text{ cm}$. $\frac{60}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times r = 22$ gives $\frac{22r}{21} = 22$, so $r = 21\text{ cm}$.

topic: Arc length
text: An arc of a circle subtends an angle of $40^\circ$ at the centre. The ratio of the length of the arc to the circumference of the circle is
answer: Correct option: C) $1:9$. Arc : circumference $= 40^\circ : 360^\circ = 1:9$.

topic: Arc length
text: A sector of a circle of radius $12\text{ cm}$ has an area of $60\text{ cm}^{2}$. The length of the arc of the sector is
answer: Correct option: D) $10\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{1}{2}lr$: $60 = \frac{1}{2}\times l\times 12$, so $l = 10\text{ cm}$.

topic: Segment area
text: A chord of a circle of radius $r$ subtends an angle of $120^\circ$ at the centre. The area of the minor segment is
answer: Correct option: B) $\frac{r^{2}}{12}(4\pi - 3\sqrt{3})$. Sector $= \frac{\pi r^{2}}{3}$; triangle $= \frac{1}{2}r^{2}\sin 120^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}r^{2}$. Segment $= \frac{\pi r^{2}}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}r^{2}}{4} = \frac{r^{2}}{12}(4\pi - 3\sqrt{3})$.

topic: Segment area
text: A chord of a circle of radius $9\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the centre. The length of the chord is
answer: Correct option: A) $9\text{ cm}$. The triangle formed by the chord and the two radii has two equal sides and a $60^\circ$ angle between them, so it is equilateral; chord $=$ radius $= 9\text{ cm}$.

topic: Segment area
text:
Assertion (A): A chord of a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the centre. The area of the minor segment is $(6\pi - 9\sqrt{3})\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Reason (R): Area of the minor segment $=$ area of the corresponding sector $-$ area of the triangle formed by the chord and the two radii.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: A) Both A and R are true and R explains A. Sector $= \frac{60}{360}\times\pi\times 36 = 6\pi$; equilateral triangle $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 36 = 9\sqrt{3}$. Segment $= 6\pi - 9\sqrt{3}$, found exactly by using R.

topic: Segment area
text: In the figure, $O$ is the centre of a circle of radius $14\text{ cm}$ and $\angle AOB = 90^\circ$. Find the perimeter of the shaded minor segment cut off by the chord $AB$. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt{2} = 1.41$)
answer:
Arc $AB = \frac{90}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14 = 22\text{ cm}$.
In right $\triangle AOB$, $AB = \sqrt{14^{2} + 14^{2}} = 14\sqrt{2} = 14\times 1.41 = 19.74\text{ cm}$.
Perimeter of segment $=$ arc $AB$ $+$ chord $AB = 22 + 19.74 = 41.74\text{ cm}$.

topic: Segment area
text: In the figure, chord $AB$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $21\text{ cm}$ subtends $\angle AOB = 120^\circ$. Take the area of $\triangle OAB$ as $191\text{ cm}^{2}$. Find (i) the perimeter of the major sector $OAB$, (ii) the area of the shaded minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
(i) Major arc $= \frac{240}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21 = \frac{2}{3}\times 132 = 88\text{ cm}$. Perimeter of major sector $= 88 + 21 + 21 = 130\text{ cm}$.
(ii) Minor sector $= \frac{120}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21\times 21 = 462\text{ cm}^{2}$. Minor segment $= 462 - 191 = 271\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Segment area
text: A chord $AB$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $20\text{ cm}$ subtends a right angle at the centre. Find (i) the length of the chord $AB$, (ii) the area of $\triangle OAB$, (iii) the area of the minor segment, (iv) the area of the major segment. (Use $\pi = 3.14$ and $\sqrt{2} = 1.41$)
answer:
(i) $AB = \sqrt{20^{2} + 20^{2}} = 20\sqrt{2} = 28.2\text{ cm}$.
(ii) Area of $\triangle OAB = \frac{1}{2}\times 20\times 20 = 200\text{ cm}^{2}$.
(iii) Minor sector $= \frac{90}{360}\times 3.14\times 400 = 314\text{ cm}^{2}$, so minor segment $= 314 - 200 = 114\text{ cm}^{2}$.
(iv) Area of circle $= 3.14\times 400 = 1256\text{ cm}^{2}$, so major segment $= 1256 - 114 = 1142\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Segment area
text: A chord $AB$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $42\text{ cm}$ subtends an angle of $60^\circ$ at the centre. Find (i) the length of the minor arc $AB$, (ii) the area of the minor segment, (iii) the perimeter of the minor segment. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
answer:
(i) Arc $AB = \frac{60}{360}\times 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 42 = 44\text{ cm}$.
(ii) Sector $OAB = \frac{60}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 42\times 42 = 924\text{ cm}^{2}$. $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral, area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 42^{2} = 441\sqrt{3} = 762.93\text{ cm}^{2}$. Minor segment $= 924 - 762.93 = 161.07\text{ cm}^{2}$.
(iii) Chord $AB = 42\text{ cm}$, so perimeter $= 44 + 42 = 86\text{ cm}$.

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: In the figure, three circles, each of radius $10\text{ cm}$, touch one another, with centres $A$, $B$ and $C$. The area of the shaded region enclosed between them is (use $\pi = 3.14$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
answer: Correct option: D) $16\text{ cm}^{2}$. $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral with side $20\text{ cm}$: area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 400 = 173\text{ cm}^{2}$. Three $60^\circ$ sectors $= \frac{180}{360}\times 3.14\times 100 = 157\text{ cm}^{2}$. Shaded $= 173 - 157 = 16\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text:
Assertion (A): The area of the ring between two concentric circles of radii $13\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$ is $25\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Reason (R): The area of the ring between concentric circles of radii $R$ and $r$ is $\pi(R - r)^{2}$.
options: Both A and R are true and R explains A
Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
answer: Correct option: C) A is true but R is false. Ring area $= \pi(13^{2} - 12^{2}) = \pi(169 - 144) = 25\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$, so A is true. The correct formula is $\pi(R^{2} - r^{2})$; $\pi(R - r)^{2}$ would give only $\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$, so R is false.

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: In the figure, $ABC$ is a triangle with $\angle A = 70^\circ$, $\angle B = 50^\circ$ and $\angle C = 60^\circ$. Sectors of radius $4\text{ cm}$ are drawn with centres $A$, $B$ and $C$. Find the total area of the three shaded sectors in terms of $\pi$.
answer:
The angles of the three sectors are the angles of the triangle, so their sum is $70^\circ + 50^\circ + 60^\circ = 180^\circ$.
Total shaded area $= \frac{180}{360}\times\pi\times 4^{2} = 8\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$.

markingSteps.step: Sum of sector angles $= 180^\circ$ (angle sum of triangle)

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: In the figure, three circles with centres $A$, $B$ and $C$, each of radius $7\text{ cm}$, touch one another. Find the area of the shaded region enclosed between the circles. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)
answer:
$AB = BC = CA = 14\text{ cm}$, so $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral: area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 14^{2} = 49\sqrt{3} = 84.77\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Each angle is $60^\circ$, so the three sectors together make $180^\circ$: area $= \frac{1}{2}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 49 = 77\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Shaded area $= 84.77 - 77 = 7.77\text{ cm}^{2}$.

markingSteps.step: Equilateral triangle of side $14\text{ cm}$, area $84.77\text{ cm}^{2}$

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: In the figure, $ABC$ is a right triangle with $\angle B = 90^\circ$, $AB = 14\text{ cm}$ and $BC = 24\text{ cm}$. A quadrant of radius $7\text{ cm}$ with centre $B$ is cut out. Find the area of the shaded region. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Area of $\triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2}\times 24\times 14 = 168\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Area of quadrant $= \frac{1}{4}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 7\times 7 = 38.5\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Shaded area $= 168 - 38.5 = 129.5\text{ cm}^{2}$.

markingSteps.step: Triangle area $= 168\text{ cm}^{2}$ and quadrant area $= 38.5\text{ cm}^{2}$

text: A school sports ground is made of a rectangle $ABCD$ with $AB = 42\text{ m}$ and $BC = 28\text{ m}$, with a semicircle on each of the shorter sides $AD$ and $BC$, as shown in the figure. A running track is marked along the outer boundary of the ground, and the whole ground is to be covered with grass. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find the area of one semicircular end.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the length of the outer boundary of the ground.
parts.answer: Two straight sides $= 2\times 42 = 84\text{ m}$; two semicircular arcs $= 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14 = 88\text{ m}$. Boundary $= 172\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the total area of the ground and the cost of grassing it at ₹ 5 per $\text{m}^{2}$.

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: Four goats are tied, one at each corner of a square field $ABCD$ of side $21\text{ m}$, each with a rope $7\text{ m}$ long, as shown in the figure. Each goat can graze only the quarter-circle region at its own corner. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find the area of the field.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Find the total area grazed by the four goats.
parts.answer: Four quadrants of radius $7\text{ m}$ make one full circle: $\frac{22}{7}\times 7\times 7 = 154\text{ m}^{2}$.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: If each rope is lengthened to $10.5\text{ m}$, find the area of the field that the goats cannot graze.
parts.answer: Ropes of $10.5\text{ m}$ from adjacent corners just meet at the midpoint of each side, so the quadrants do not overlap. Grazed $= \frac{22}{7}\times 10.5\times 10.5 = 346.5\text{ m}^{2}$. Ungrazed $= 441 - 346.5 = 94.5\text{ m}^{2}$.

topic: Combination figures (shaded regions)
text: For a sports-day display, a circle is marked on the ground using a rope $132\text{ m}$ long laid along its boundary. From the centre $O$, two straight ropes $OA$ and $OB$ are laid to the boundary and a third rope $AB$ is laid so that $\triangle OAB$ is equilateral. The segment between chord $AB$ and the arc $AB$ is painted, as shown in the figure. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ and $\sqrt{3} = 1.73$)

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Find the radius of the circle.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Find the area of the painted segment.
parts.answer: Sector $= \frac{60}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 21\times 21 = 231\text{ m}^{2}$. Triangle $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\times 441 = 190.73\text{ m}^{2}$. Segment $= 231 - 190.73 = 40.27\text{ m}^{2}$.

topic: Wheel, clock, garden and wiper contexts
text: The angle turned through by the hour hand of a clock from 10:00 am to 3:30 pm on the same day is
answer: Correct option: B) $165^\circ$. The hour hand turns $30^\circ$ per hour; from 10:00 am to 3:30 pm is $5.5$ hours, so $5.5\times 30^\circ = 165^\circ$.

topic: Wheel, clock, garden and wiper contexts
text: The wheel of a cart makes $250$ complete revolutions in covering a distance of $550\text{ m}$. The diameter of the wheel is (use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer: Correct option: C) $70\text{ cm}$. Circumference $= \frac{550}{250} = 2.2\text{ m} = 220\text{ cm}$. $\pi d = 220$ gives $d = 220\times\frac{7}{22} = 70\text{ cm}$.

topic: Wheel, clock, garden and wiper contexts
text: The hour hand of a wall clock is $14\text{ cm}$ long. Find the area swept by it from $12$ noon to $3$ pm, and the area of the corresponding major sector of the clock face it traces. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
In $3$ hours the hour hand turns $3\times 30^\circ = 90^\circ$.
Minor sector $= \frac{90}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14\times 14 = 154\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Circle $= 616\text{ cm}^{2}$, so major sector $= 616 - 154 = 462\text{ cm}^{2}$.

verification.note: Wording 'major sector of the clock face it traces' is slightly awkward (clock face may be larger than the 14 cm hand), but 'it traces' fixes radius 14; key 154 / 462 cm² correct.

topic: Wheel, clock, garden and wiper contexts
text: A bus has two windscreen wipers that do not overlap. Each wiper has a blade of length $35\text{ cm}$ and sweeps through an angle of $72^\circ$. Find the total area cleaned at each sweep of the two blades. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
Area cleaned by one blade $= \frac{72}{360}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 35\times 35 = \frac{1}{5}\times 3850 = 770\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Total for two blades $= 2\times 770 = 1540\text{ cm}^{2}$.

topic: Wheel, clock, garden and wiper contexts
text: A horse is tied to a peg at one corner of a square-shaped grass field of side $35\text{ m}$ by a rope $14\text{ m}$ long. Find (i) the area of the part of the field in which the horse can graze, (ii) the increase in the grazing area if the rope is replaced by one $28\text{ m}$ long, (iii) the area of the field the horse still cannot graze with the longer rope. (Use $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$)
answer:
(i) The horse grazes a quadrant of radius $14\text{ m}$ (angle of the square $= 90^\circ$): area $= \frac{1}{4}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 14\times 14 = 154\text{ m}^{2}$.
(ii) With a $28\text{ m}$ rope (still shorter than the side $35\text{ m}$, so the quadrant stays inside the field): area $= \frac{1}{4}\times\frac{22}{7}\times 28\times 28 = 616\text{ m}^{2}$. Increase $= 616 - 154 = 462\text{ m}^{2}$.
(iii) Field $= 35\times 35 = 1225\text{ m}^{2}$. Ungrazed $= 1225 - 616 = 609\text{ m}^{2}$.

markingSteps.step: Recognising the grazed region as a quadrant of radius $14\text{ m}$

parts.text: Find the circumference of the park.
